channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Example: 'public_channel,private_channel,im'

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 1000 (maximum 999).

query.description: Optional keyword to filter channels. Case-insensitive substring match against the fields specified by query_targets. Example: 'marketing' returns channels like #marketing, #marketing-ops.

query_targets.description: Comma-separated list of fields to match the query against. Allowed values: 'name', 'topic', 'purpose'. Example: 'name,topic,purpose' to search all fields. Default is 'name'.

sort.description: Type of sorting. Allowed values: 'popularity' - sort by number of members/participants in each channel.

tools.name: channels_me
tools.description: List channels you are a member of. Unlike channels_list which returns all workspace channels, this returns only channels you have joined. Useful on large workspaces where channels_list returns thousands of results.

channel_types.description: Comma-separated channel types. Allowed values: 'mpim', 'im', 'public_channel', 'private_channel'. Default: 'public_channel,private_channel'.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-999).

tools.name: conversations_add_message
tools.description: Add a message to a public channel, private channel, or direct message (DM, or IM) conversation by channel_id and thread_ts.

blocks.description: Raw Slack Block Kit JSON array for rich message formatting (rich_text lists, code blocks, etc.). When provided, this takes precedence over text/content_type for rendering. The text parameter becomes the notification fallback text.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

content_type.description: Content type of the message. Default is 'text/markdown'. Allowed values: 'text/markdown', 'text/plain'. Ignored when blocks is provided.

text.description: Message text in specified content_type format. Example: 'Hello, world!' for text/plain or '# Hello, world!' for text/markdown.

thread_ts.description: Unique identifier of either a thread's parent message or a message in the thread_ts must be the timestamp in format 1234567890.123456 of an existing message with 0 or more replies. Optional, if not provided the message will be added to the channel itself, otherwise it will be added to the thread.

tools.name: conversations_history
tools.description: Get messages from the channel (or DM) by channel_id, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: - `channel_id` (string): ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 1w - 1 week, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

tools.name: conversations_join
tools.description: Join a public channel. Use channels_list or channels_me to find channel IDs.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... (e.g., #general).

tools.name: conversations_leave
tools.description: Leave a channel, group conversation, or DM. Cannot leave the #general channel.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

tools.name: conversations_mark
tools.description: Mark a channel or DM as read. If no timestamp is provided, marks all messages as read.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... (e.g., #general, @username).

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to mark as read up to. If not provided, marks all messages as read.

tools.name: conversations_replies
tools.description: Get a thread of messages posted to a conversation by channelID and thread_ts, the last row/column in the response is used as 'cursor' parameter for pagination if not empty

channel_id.description: ID of the channel in format Cxxxxxxxxxx or its name starting with #... or @... aka #general or @username_dm.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

include_activity_messages.description: If true, the response will include activity messages such as 'channel_join' or 'channel_leave'. Default is boolean false.

limit.description: Limit of messages to fetch in format of maximum ranges of time (e.g. 1d - 1 day, 30d - 30 days, 90d - 90 days which is a default limit for free tier history) or number of messages (e.g. 50). Must be empty when 'cursor' is provided.

thread_ts.description: Unique identifier of either a thread's parent message or a message in the thread. ts must be the timestamp in format 1234567890.123456 of an existing message with 0 or more replies.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages in a public channel, private channel, or direct message (DM, or IM) conversation using filters. All filters are optional, if not provided then search_query is required.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value of the last row and column in the response as next_cursor field returned from the previous request.

filter_date_after.description: Filter messages sent after a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_before.description: Filter messages sent before a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_during.description: Filter messages sent during a specific period in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_date_on.description: Filter messages sent on a specific date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Example: '2023-10-01', 'July', 'Yesterday' or 'Today'. If not provided, all dates will be searched.

filter_in_channel.description: Filter messages in a specific public/private channel by its ID or name. Example: 'C1234567890', 'G1234567890', or '#general'. If not provided, all channels will be searched.

filter_in_im_or_mpim.description: Filter messages in a direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPIM) conversation by its ID or name. Example: 'D1234567890' or '@username_dm'. If not provided, all DMs and MPIMs will be searched.

filter_threads_only.description: If true, the response will include only messages from threads. Default is boolean false.

filter_users_from.description: Filter messages from a specific user by their ID or display name. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all users will be searched.

filter_users_with.description: Filter messages with a specific user by their ID or display name in threads and DMs. Example: 'U1234567890' or '@username'. If not provided, all threads and DMs will be searched.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

search_query.description: Search query to filter messages. Example: 'marketing report' or full URL of Slack message e.g. 'https://slack.com/archives/C1234567890/p1234567890123456', then the tool will return a single message matching given URL, herewith all other parameters will be ignored.

tools.name: conversations_unreads
tools.description: Get unread messages across all channels. With browser session tokens (xoxc/xoxd), uses a single API call for complete results. With OAuth user tokens (xoxp), scans a subset of channels per type (limited by max_channels) — results may be partial on large workspaces. Results are prioritized: DMs > group DMs > partner channels > internal channels.

channel_types.description: Filter by channel type: 'all' (default), 'dm' (direct messages), 'group_dm' (group DMs), 'partner' (ext-* channels), 'internal' (other channels).

include_messages.description: If true (default), returns the actual unread messages. If false, returns only a summary of channels with unreads.

include_muted.description: If true, includes muted channels in results. Default is false (muted channels are excluded, matching Slack app behavior).

max_channels.description: Maximum number of channels to fetch unreads from. Default is 50.

max_messages_per_channel.description: Maximum messages to fetch per channel. Default is 10.

mentions_only.description: If true, only returns channels where you have @mentions. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_create
tools.description: Create a new user group (mention group) in the Slack workspace. After creation, use usergroups_users_update to add members, or users can join themselves with usergroups_me. The handle becomes the @mention (e.g., handle='engineering' creates @engineering).

channels.description: Comma-separated channel IDs where this group is commonly mentioned. Members get suggestions to join these channels.

description.description: Purpose or description shown in group details (e.g., 'Backend and frontend engineers').

handle.description: The @mention handle without the @ symbol (e.g., 'engineering' for @engineering). Keep it short and lowercase. If omitted, Slack auto-generates one from the name.

name.description: Display name of the user group (e.g., 'Engineering Team', 'Design Squad').

tools.name: usergroups_list
tools.description: List all user groups (subteams) in the Slack workspace. User groups are mention groups like @engineering or @design that notify all members. Use this to discover available groups, check group membership counts, or find a group's ID before joining/updating it. Returns CSV with columns: id, name, handle, description, user_count, is_external.

include_count.description: Include user count for each group. Default is true.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled/archived groups. Default is false.

include_users.description: Include list of user IDs in each group. Default is false.

tools.name: usergroups_me
tools.description: Manage your own user group membership. Use action='list' to see which groups you belong to. Use action='join' with a usergroup_id to add yourself to a group (e.g., to receive @mentions). Use action='leave' with a usergroup_id to remove yourself. This is the easiest way to join/leave groups without needing to know the full member list.

action.description: Action to perform: 'list' returns CSV of groups you're a member of, 'join' adds you to a group, 'leave' removes you from a group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Required for 'join' and 'leave' actions. Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_update
tools.description: Update a user group's metadata: name, handle (@mention), description, or default channels. Does NOT change members - use usergroups_users_update for that. At least one field must be provided.

channels.description: New default channel IDs (comma-separated). Replaces existing default channels.

handle.description: New @mention handle (without @). Changing this changes how users mention the group.

name.description: New display name for the group.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group to update (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

tools.name: usergroups_users_update
tools.description: Replace all members of a user group with a new list. WARNING: This completely replaces the member list - any user not in the 'users' parameter will be removed. To add/remove just yourself, use usergroups_me instead. To add a single user without removing others, first get current members from usergroups_list with include_users=true, then call this with the combined list.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the user group (starts with 'S', e.g., 'S0123456789'). Get IDs from usergroups_list.

users.description: Comma-separated user IDs that will become the COMPLETE member list (e.g., 'U0123456789,U9876543210'). All current members not in this list will be removed.

tools.name: users_search
tools.description: Search for users by name, email, display name, or Slack user ID. If a Slack user ID is provided (e.g. U07VCEPP4N5), the user is looked up directly. Returns user details and DM channel ID if available.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default is 10.

query.description: Search query - matches against real name, display name, username, email, or a Slack user ID (e.g. U07VCEPP4N5).
